content_html_sanitized:
There are almost 18,000 different law enforcement agencies in the United States.

 

Obviously, with such a variety of sizes and locations, these organizations vary greatly in every way. However, it would appear that an overwhelming majority have been institutionally opposed to marijuana legalization.

 

As with some psychiatrists and other opponents of legalization, they conflate their areas of supposed expertise with the effects of legalization in society, a socioeconomic question.

See

Politicized Psychiatry Is Insane

And

Politicized Psychiatry and the Rehab Rackets

 

Psychiatrists who are supposedly experts in mental health, are not experts in social and economic policies. Law enforcement officials are experts on police procedures which are extremely important and often dangerous, but also are not experts in social and economic policies.

 

Both of these very different groups are necessarily involved with the problems associated with the human condition. Psychiatrists and the police, like emergency room physicians, see people with problems. If all a person knew about automobiles was based on emergency room experiences, automobile prohibition might seem essential.

 

Also, the police were both authorized and required by the Congress and the state legislatures to enforce these laws. However, when the appropriateness of the laws are questioned, the Prohibitionists in the legislatures, who are usually not experts on anything other than getting reelected, will invite the police to testify as to the necessity of the laws. Obviously, this is a circular process.

 

However, law enforcement has become more professional and the experience of police agencies in states with legalization has demonstrated that the world did not come to an end.
